requirement_lines: # Client / Chart Data Model v1
**CANONICAL** for non-AI Web 2.0 product data architecture.
**Scope:** Entity model, persistence boundaries, saved exploration shape, active context, and optional post-v1 behavioral capture — **documentation only**. Not SQL. Not implementation.
**Filename convention:** New dated docs put the date at the **end** of the filename (e.g. `client_chart_data_model_v1_2026-05-29.md`). Older files are not renamed by this document.

**Reads with:** `docs/constitutional/map_first_product_doctrine_v1.md` (**product identity authority**), `docs/ux/2026-05-29_application_journey_architecture_v1.md`, `docs/data_model/local_first_data_objects_v1.md`, `docs/data_model/local_product_store_v2.md`, `docs/data_model/supabase_schema_sandbox_plan_v1.md`.
Define the **non-AI Web 2.0 product data model** for the relocation app, aligned with the current UX journey doctrine.
- what must never be persisted as product truth,
- what is explicitly **out of scope** for the current product generation.
The model supports **exploration, refinement, evaluation, and decision-making** — not administration theater, not oracle closure, not AI-derived meaning.
Saved Searches (saved explorations)

Favorites and Comparison Sets are **high continuity value**. Saved Searches are **lower prominence** comfort/resume objects. History stores behavioral facts for archive/clear — not primary navigation.
│  PRODUCT RECORDS (Web 2.0 — local-first → future sync)       │
│  Account · Chart Record · Place · Favorite · SavedExploration│
│  · ComparisonSet · inline notes · History (per Chart Record) │
│ must not persist as authority
│  GeoJSON fragments · canvas · aura · debug substrate         │
| Term | Meaning in Web 2.0 |
| **Chart Record** | Preferred neutral name for the primary user-owned natal identity + professional label. One natal chart per record. |
| **Client** | UI/product language for a Chart Record when the professional workflow treats the subject as a client. **Synonym in current scope**, not a separate entity with multiple charts. |
| **Birth profile** | Natal input domain (date, time, place, timezone). **1:1 with Chart Record** in current scope. |
| **Place** | Stable geographic identity (geoname / WOF-style ID when available + lat/lon). |
| **Saved exploration** | Durable saved search / investigation session (conditions + map context + interaction facts). |
| **Comparison Set** | 2–5 **saved places / locations** compared under **one** Chart Record — not multi-chart comparison. |
Long-term, **Chart Record** may supersede **Client** in schema naming where the record is not literally a paying client (research chart, self-chart). Current UI may still say “client.”
| **Chart Record** | User-facing **client / chart / research** record — one active natal identity per row |
| `chartRecordId` | Often `client.id` in JSON/SQL |
| Inline `notes` on record / favorite / exploration | Canonical Web 2.0 — not a separate `notes` table yet |

**Rule:** Product language may say “client.” Data architecture treats each row as **one Chart Record** with exactly one birth profile in Web 2.0. Internal schemas may split `clients` + `birth_profiles` for normalization; do not infer multiple charts per client from that split.
# 1. Chart Record / client model
**One Chart Record = one natal chart = one active client/research identity.** No multiple charts inside one record in the current Web 2.0 product.

**Web 2.0 ownership rule:** Favorites, inline notes, saved explorations, map/search history, and comparison sets belong to **exactly one Chart Record**. There is no shared favorite pool, note namespace, or history bucket across records except at account settings (e.g. global defaults, clear-all-history as lower priority).
| One birth profile per Chart Record | Nested chart list on one client |
| Separate Chart Records for distinct natal identities | Composite chart as child of client |
| Professional display name + inline notes on the record | Rectified alternate time as sibling chart under same client |
| User-declared `confidenceTier` + optional metadata | AI-inferred birth time stored as exact time |

If the user needs a **distinct natal identity** — **research chart**, **composite chart** (future), **solar chart policy record** (future), etc. — each is created as a **separate Chart Record** (client-like row), not as a nested chart collection.

**Relocated event charts are not a Web 2.0 MVP use case.** Edge cases belong under **`record_type: research`** without event-chart product UX or storage typing. Dedicated event-chart support remains a future box only (see §11 exclusions).

**Not separate Chart Records:** birth-time uncertainty variants, rectification candidates, or bounded-range hypotheses. Those belong to **one user-facing Chart Record** as internal metadata / future internal calculation domains — see birth-time sections below. **Rectification workflow is out of scope** for Web 2.0.
**Rationale:** Keeps active context, favorites, saved explorations, and map ownership unambiguous. Avoids selector complexity and hidden chart switching in MVP.
| `accountId` | yes | Owning professional account |
| `displayName` | yes | Professional label (“Anna Rivera”, “Research — Solstice reference”) |
| `recordType` | yes | Web 2.0: **`self`**, **`client`**, **`research`** only — not `event` |
| `birthTime` | yes / nullable | Nullable only with honest unknown-time or bounded-range policy — see below |
### Optional demographic / profile metadata (future only)

Optional fields such as **gender** or similar demographic profile metadata may later support **AI interpretation layers** (post–Web 2.0). They are **not required** for Dumb Web 2.0 and **must not affect Layer 1 geometry** or relocation truth computation. Do not model, require, or surface in MVP UI unless explicitly approved in a future slice.
### Birth time confidence — in scope vs excluded (Web 2.0)
| In scope (storage) | Excluded (Web 2.0) |
| Honest display of tier on client, map, popup, comparison, export | AI birth-time **inference** stored as fact |
Aligns with `docs/future/birth_time_uncertainty_and_confidence_doctrine.md` for **recording and surfacing** tier; does not implement rectification or AI intake.
Candidate Location Chart (favorites, map picks, comparison cards)
| Rule | Detail |
| Chart Page | Must surface **Current Location Chart** alongside Birth Chart — not buried in header copy |
| Comparison | Current Location may appear as **preset comparison anchor** (with Natal) from Chart Page |
| Baseline role | Often the reference against which relocation candidates are measured |
| Rule | Detail |
| Field | `intentSummary` (plain text or structured stub — implementation TBD) |
| Status | **Reserved** — may remain empty in V1 |
| Intent IS NOT | Walkability, airports, cost, politics, ocean, climate — Layer 5 city intelligence, post-astro |
| Future sources | AI intake (auditable output), professional edit, manual user authorship |
| Visibility | Must be **visible and auditable** when populated — not hidden in AI memory only |
Aligns with `docs/constitutional/map_first_product_doctrine_v1.md` and Layer 3 vs Layer 5 in `docs/ai/ai_interpretation_truthfulness_doctrine_v1_2026-05-30.md`.
### Unknown birth time (Web 2.0)
**Unknown birth time means relocation chart cannot be run honestly.** Houses and angles are time-sensitive; the app must **not fake precision**.
- Do **not** present relocation overlays or point truth as authoritative without explicit solar-chart or documented policy watermark.
- Route the user to **guidance**: find birth records, ask family, obtain bounded approximate range — not to silent defaults masquerading as exact.
- Nullable `birthTime` is allowed **only** with visible tier/policy — never an invisible noon chart.
- **Very broad uncertainty** should route the user toward finding better birth-time records — not toward pretending a single exact time.
### Ambiguous / bounded birth time (future box only)
│  FUTURE: Birth-time uncertainty gradient      │
│  Post–Web 2.0 AI may support user-indicated   │

requirement_lines: # Intentionality and symbolic constraints
**Status:** Durable **institutional philosophy** and **future AI-governance** doctrine.

**Purpose:** State clearly how this product thinks about **fate**, **agency**, **relocation**, **tradeoffs**, and **intentionality** so implementation, copy, and interpretive systems do not drift toward manipulative spirituality, false certainty, or infinite malleability.
- **`ai_context/core_product_truths.md`** — parallel **interpretive integrity** and **tradeoff intelligence** sections.
- **`docs/institutional_memory_synthesis.md`** — §4 **Interpretive integrity and archetypal honesty** (bridge + AI-governed surfaces).
- **`docs/visual_semantic_style_guide.md`** — **truth hierarchy** (popup / overlay / account): symbolic exploration on the map must stay **accountable** to structure.
- **`ai_context/memory_workflow.md`** — how proposals are reviewed and promoted so chat drift does not override this doctrine.

- **Archetypes and placements keep their weight:** difficult configurations are not rhetorically dissolved. **Saturn remains Saturn;** harsh or limiting symbolism is not reframed as secretly benefic to soothe the user.
- **Astrology is not “manifestation culture.”** The product rejects the implication that belief or wording alone reshuffles symbolic structure without cost or constraint.
**Product consequence:** Math, overlays, and popups must remain **honest** about membership and relocated facts; interpretive layers must not **contradict** point truth for comfort.
## 2. Agency exists within constraints (relocation reframed)
- **Some environments support certain expressions better than others.** Geography changes **angles, houses, and local combinations**; it does not erase the natal pattern wholesale.

**Product consequence:** Comparison and search UX should eventually support **intentional optimization** (e.g. constrained city sets, explicit priorities) without promising **universal “best place on Earth.”**

- **Illustrative pattern:** A **Sun–angle relationship in a practical, sustaining city** may be preferable to a **Sun-heavy emphasis** that only shines in a place the user cannot actually build a life in. The tool should **hold** that comparison without collapsing it into “which line is prettier on the map.”

- **Relocation is symbolic optimization under realism:** logistics, law, relationships, and economics remain **outside** the chart but **inside** adult decision-making; the software does not pretend otherwise.
**Product consequence:** Future **comparison** and **assist** features should encode **tradeoff language** as first-class—not as a single “winner” badge.
- **Positive framing must not erase symbolic structure.** Warmth in tone is compatible with **honesty about difficulty**; **toxic positivity** is not.
- **Asymmetry stays** in interpretations: symmetric “everything is equally fine” copy is a **failure mode** for relocation astrology.
## 5. Dynamic participation (between fatalism and naive free will)
- **Paradox and openness** are preserved: the user is invited to **live inside** uncertain, multi-valued symbolic space—not to receive a closed verdict from software.
**Product consequence:** Language (human or AI) should allow **maturity** and **unfinishedness**; closure is for **logistics**, not for **meaning** at gunpoint.
## 6. AI interpretation implications (governance)
**Architecture and reviewer doctrine:** **`docs/ai_constitution_and_review_architecture.md`** (layers, drift risks, anti-patterns, reviewer checks).
AI and assistive systems **must**:
- **Lead with astrology, follow with narrative:** chart logic **constraints** generated copy; the user supplies **biography, values, and culture.**
AI **must not** (see also **`docs/institutional_memory_synthesis.md`** §4):
- **Treat the latest chat tone** as superseding **`ai_context/`** and **`docs/`** doctrine—**reviewer and memory workflows** exist to prevent that drift (`ai_context/memory_workflow.md`).

- **Skepticism-friendly:** users tired of **manipulative spirituality**, **false certainty**, and **cosmic hype** should recognize the product as **restrained** and **truth-hierarchy clear** (`docs/visual_semantic_style_guide.md` §1).

- **The map is not passive fate consumption.** It is an **instrument for browsing symbolic geography**—overlays **suggest where to look**; **popups and future account surfaces** **settle** what holds at a place (`docs/visual_semantic_style_guide.md`).
- **The user actively explores possible symbolic environments** and plausible futures; the software **does not** decide their life for them.
Any future feature that **interprets** placements, **compares** cities, or **assists** professionals/consumers should be checked against:
3. **`ai_context/core_product_truths.md`** (parallel interpretive doctrine),
4. **`docs/ai_constitution_and_review_architecture.md`** (governance layers, reviewer duties, anti-patterns),

before ship. **Epistemic** truth (math, popups, overlays) stays governed by **`docs/visual_semantic_style_guide.md`** and technical validation docs; **this** file governs **meaning, tone, and agency claims** layered on top.

- **Chat memory** is high-context and ephemeral. Without promotion to repo files, it **vanishes** and the next session invents fresh “facts.”
- **Project memory** (`ai_context/`, `docs/`, themed consolidated notes) is **slow, deliberate, and reconciled to the codebase**—the antidote to treating the latest model reply as law.
- Reconcile claims against **git and running modules** before refactoring (“which `main` is live?”).
- **Human visual QA** remains authoritative for map topology even when screenshots or agents say “looks fine.”
## AI reviewer infrastructure (evolution)
- **Direction in archaeology:** reviewer prompts should carry **exact scripts, expected outputs, and hypotheses**; screenshots alone are fragile.
- **Tension:** richer context vs review noise—see `ai_context/open_questions.md` (reviewer scope, archive strategy).
- **Professional tool first:** accounts/clients/comparisons/export are the serious “work surface,” not just a map gimmick.
- **Non-AI / “dumb mode” remains sacred:** the app must be fully usable without automated interpretation—professional sovereignty matters ethically and commercially.
- **AI is augmentation, not authority:** aids with alternatives, intake translation, summaries—does not replace judgment.
## AI collaboration failures as institutional risk
Repeated “AI solved the wrong problem” catalog includes:
- editing `main.py` while server runs another module
- Cross-model review (e.g., implementation vs review) can rescue indentation/architecture mistakes, but prompts must include **exact scripts, expected outputs, and hypotheses**—not screenshots alone.
## Practitioner assist vision (future)
“Nudges” when constraints are impossible (offer nearby alternatives; suggest angle/house substitutions) appear as high-value professional features *after* the map engine is trusted.
## Consumer / intake AI (later)

DeepSeek extracts include **white-label / B2B adjacent services** framing and tiered monetization stories. Useful for understanding founder intent; must be reviewed against actual product ethics, scope, and legal positioning before adoption as public roadmap.

Some archaeology markets the system as **“geospatial decision intelligence”** more broadly than astrology. That may be a positioning lens—or overclaim—depending on product ethics and regulatory context. Keep as **narrative tension**, not silent merge into public docs without human review.

requirement_lines: # Relocation App Product Roadmap
This document preserves the current product strategy, development sequence, UX philosophy, and validation priorities for future work.
The app has reached an important early professional-tool milestone:
- `truth_grid` house overlays are working and remain opt-in.
- Staged/shared-grid ASC overlays are working.
- The app is now viable as an early professional astrology exploration tool, pending UX cleanup and broader fixture testing.
- `truth_grid` is not yet default.
- The `+/-65` latitude cap remains in place.
The app should be a map-first experience. The map is the product surface; controls exist to serve exploration, not dominate it.
- The environment should feel professional-grade, calm, inviting, premium, restrained, and trustworthy.
- Users should enjoy spending time in the app.
- Visual design should communicate confidence without becoming flashy.
- Controls should make exploration easier, not compete with the map.
- Professional users need power, but not clutter.
The app should feel like a refined professional instrument, not a dashboard full of gimmicks.
Important domain note:
Future search types:
## 4. Overlay/Color System Roadmap
Overlap is the answer. Overlap regions are the "shopping cart" of candidate cities: the map should make it obvious where multiple desired conditions coincide.
- Overlap regions must be visually explicit.
- Overlays must stay transparent enough to read map labels and cities.
- Avoid naive alpha stacking when it makes purple or dark colors dominate.
- Overlap can be brighter or more luminous, but should not simply become more opaque.
- Search controls should eventually reflect the selected overlay color, so the UI itself acts as the legend.
- The current legend is too space-consuming and should eventually be removed or replaced.
Color families should distinguish:
- Should not light up the whole inverse region.
- Should use subtle grey, black, desaturated, or "off limits" treatment.
- Should communicate constraint without visually overwhelming positive search intent.
- The color system should become theme-aware for light/dark maps.
- Color semantics should remain readable for colorblind users.
- Overlap treatment should scale to multi-condition searches without visual mud.
## 5. Aspect Aura Roadmap
The next visual layer should add a frontend-rendered aura/intensity field around ASC/MC aspect lines:
- Aura should not look like a fat speed bump.
- Aura should be subtle at the outer edge and intensify sharply/nonlinearly toward the centerline.
- The centerline remains the darkest/strongest point.
- Aura shows "extra juice" inside broader house/sign regions.
- Backend should remain the source of exact centerlines.
- Aspect aura shows intensified angular contact inside or across those regions.
- The aura should help professional users quickly see where a city is close enough to matter without pretending every part of a broad band has equal strength.
## 6. UX/Layout Roadmap
- Dropdown auto-advance behavior still exists and must be fixed.
- User-facing status text such as "Angular overlay ready" should not remain in its current form.
- Debug badge should remain debug-only.

- The map is the primary visual instrument, but account, intake, comparison, and settings screens may define the soul and tone of the app because they contain more traditional interface design and long-form user interaction.
- They should establish the app's premium, calm, elegant design language.
- The map control drawer/genie should grow out of that design language, not precede it as an isolated clever interaction.
- The map should dominate.
- Controls should collapse or retract elegantly.
- Restore-control affordance must be obvious if controls are hidden.
- Mobile, tablet, ultrawide, and narrow desktop layouts must be considered.
- Controls should be discoverable and calm, not buried.
- The app should teach interaction affordances once, then get out of the way.
## 7. City Search / Geocoder Roadmap
- Atlanta, Georgia should rank before obscure Atlanta variants.
Future geocoder direction:
- The geocoder should be much smarter than the current local city list.
- It should support ambiguity gracefully rather than pretending the first match is always right.
- It should eventually combine local curated data with a stronger geocoding source.
- City density should be based on visible map density and user relevance, not only raw population.
## 8. Birth Data / Accounts / Professional Mode Roadmap
Accounts are eventually needed, but not before the professional core stabilizes.
Future design areas:
- Saved charts.
- Comparison workspace.
- Later uncertain birth time intake.
- Professional/dumb mode vs AI-assisted mode.
- These screens should carry the app's premium design language.
- They should be calm and beautiful, not merely administrative.

requirement_lines: **Status labels:** *Durable principle* = should guide decisions for years. *Product stance* = strategic positioning. *Process principle* = how the team builds.

- **Durable principle — Inspectable precision:** If the map shows a region, line, or overlap, it must mean something **precise** in the relocated chart model. “Plausible geometry” is not validation. Trust is built through reproducible checks, not visual confidence.
- **Durable principle — The map is the primary model (not an illustration):** Users explore **geography as astrology**. The map is not decoration around a chart calculator; it is the main instrument.

- **Product stance — Not generic astrocartography:** The ambition is a **multi-condition, overlap-aware relocation exploration tool** reframing the category toward *relocation astrology* and *intent-driven comparisons*, not only angle lines on a globe.
- **Durable principle — Professional rigor before lay simplification:** Build a **neutral, powerful professional engine first**; simplify for lay users only after the foundation is trustworthy.

- **Durable principle — Tradeoffs are inherent:** “Best place on Earth” is usually the wrong framing. The tool should help users clarify priorities and compare **constrained** options (e.g. three company cities), not imply one universal optimum.
- **Durable principle — Binary regions must be honest:** House membership and angle-sign membership are effectively **in/out** for users. False membership is unacceptable even in MVP.

- **Durable principle — Cosmetic roughness can be acceptable:** Seam cosmetics, visible discontinuities, and imperfect basemap styling can be acceptable **if canonical membership remains correct** and inspectable.

- **Durable principle — Aspect intensity is continuous:** Exact aspect-to-angle **centerlines** are mathematical anchors; **auras/orbs** express continuous strength and can be softer—*but must not lie about exactness at the core*.

- **Durable principle — Math vs rendering diagnosis:** Errors must be classified: astrology math vs GeoJSON vs map interaction vs stale server vs wrong file vs race conditions vs **AI instruction ambiguity**. Mixing categories wastes weeks.
## Human + AI collaboration stance
- **Process principle — AI assists; humans validate:** Especially for map truth, AI can speed implementation but cannot become the authority that overrides chart checks.
- **Process principle — Surgical vs strategic modes:** During debugging, the user repeatedly needed **ordered surgical steps**, not architectural musings. Mismatch of mode caused major failures.
- **Product stance — Calm, premium restraint:** “Inevitable, not clever.” Long-session comfort matters. Avoid gimmicks, neon toy UX, and astrology hype.

- **Continuity note (archaeology):** Technical choices that reduce **false certainty** and **opaque blocking** (e.g. staged rendering, inspectable truth, honest membership) align with the same emotional contract—users should trust the instrument over multiple long sessions, not chase a flashy map that lies or “freezes” until magic finishes.

14. Key tensions and balancing acts (do not flatten)
requirement_lines: **Status:** Foundational doctrine for **future training**, **reviewer systems**, **UX design**, **product strategy**, **conversational architecture**, and **interpretive governance**.

**Authority:** Synthesizes durable texts in `ai_context/`, `docs/`, and `memory_archaeology_raw/consolidated_notes/`. It **does not** supersede those sources on technical implementation; it **weaves** them into one training-readable whole.

This posture has a deliberate audience: **astrology for grownups**—intellectually serious, skepticism-friendly, **sober without cynicism**. Warmth is expressed through **restraint**, not through neon spiritual retail. Excitement is expected to arise from **exploration and judgment on the instrument**, not from UI theatrics, cosmic clickbait, or model cheerleading. The map is the **primary visual model**, not wallpaper behind forms. Overlap of conditions—house plus house, house plus angle-in-sign, corridors of aspect logic—is treated as a **semantic object** worth designing for, not an accident of stacking transparent colors.

Underneath lies a technical moral that keeps philosophy honest: **inspectable precision**. If the map shows a region or line, it must mean something **precise** in the relocated model. “Plausible-looking geometry” is not validation. **False membership** is rejected even when cosmetics are rough; **rough edges** can be acceptable when membership stays true and **popups remain authoritative**. Beauty is supposed to **emerge from truthful systems**—but beauty that **lies** (blur that smuggles category, opacity that fakes inside/outside) is worse than rough honesty.

**Practical implication:** Institutional decisions should always ask two questions: (1) Does this preserve **symbolic and mathematical integrity** at the point of contact with the user? (2) Does this preserve **room for the user’s intention, biography, and cultural context**—which the software does not possess?

The product aligns with **symbolic realism**: archetypes, houses, angles, and aspects carry **weight** and **friction**. **Saturn remains Saturn**; difficult configurations are not rhetorically dissolved into generic growth branding. **Positive framing** is compatible with honesty; **toxic positivity** is not. The system refuses the symmetrical lie that “everything is equally fine,” because relocation astrology’s value is **asymmetric comparison**: some signatures are harder, some relocations buy relief at a cost elsewhere, and **double or triple wins** (where they exist) deserve to be visible **without** erasing tensions where the chart is genuinely conflicted.
- **Account / chart surfaces** (future-facing in fullness) carry the **full record**—dense tables, comparisons, exports, professional readouts.

Popups are **dense shorthand**, not spreadsheet-on-map; they settle local truth **without** pretending to be the entire counseling session. Aura, gradients, and planned cusp softness are **display semantics** with strict contracts: they must **not** contradict popup membership at the same point. The **centerline** of an aspect-to-angle construction is an exact anchor; **orb-space intensity** may be softer but cannot gaslight exactness.
Two visual metaphors must remain **distinct** in both engineering and user education:
- **House cusp transition (~order of 2° in planning doctrine):** categorical **house membership** with **presentational** softness at boundaries—not the same as epistemic “we don’t know.”
- **Aspect-to-angle aura (~5–8° bands, aspect-tunable in product imagination):** **angular** intensity toward exactness—not house-to-house category bleed.
### 2.4 Dynamic participation (between fatalism and naive will)

The philosophy explicitly refuses two default stories: **rigid fatalism** (“nothing you do matters”) and **simplistic free-will absolutism** (“you can be anyone anywhere with the right mindset”). Relocation is **material constraint + symbolic constraint + human logistics**. The growth impulse—the desire to move, revise, transcend—may itself be **richly readable** in a chart without being over-celebrated as guaranteed transcendence. **Paradox and openness** are treated as features: the user is invited to **live inside multi-valued symbolic space**, not receive **forensic closure** from software meant to optimize a lunch order.

**Practical implication:** Language (human or AI) should tolerate **maturity** and **unfinishedness**. Closure belongs to **logistics and UI affordances** (“this query returned three candidate cells”); closure does not belong to **meaning at gunpoint**.
## 3. AI behavioral doctrine

AI is positioned as **navigation assistance** within chart structure—not as **guru**, **oracle**, or **replacement parent**. The institution expects interpretive systems to **lead with astrology and follow with narrative**: chart logic **constrains** generated language; the user supplies **biography, values, culture, and agency**.

The behavioral bar is **archetypal honesty**: assists may **contextualize, integrate, strategize, compensate, redirect**—they may not **wish difficulty away**, **relabel** Saturn into abundance branding, or **flatten** a chart into one emotional temperature. **Recognition** is preferred over **surprise theater**: strong readings produce the feeling “this architecture matches my life” rather than manufactured astonishment, fabricated micro-biography, or intimacies the model cannot ethically claim.

Because modern LLMs **systemically drift** toward likability, the doctrine treats **comfort bias** as a **predictable hazard**, not a personal failure of a vendor. Flattery, certainty inflation, emotional smoothing, fake positivity, over-specificity, dependency framing, pseudo-mysticism, and urgency hooks are catalogued as **failure modes** to be caught—**not** as “good UX” if users feel briefly soothed.

**GPS metaphor (institutional):** When AI is allowed to speak about relocation paths, the preferred mental model is **recalculating route**, not **prophecy**. The user sets constraints (relationship geography, legal reality, career corridors). The system proposes **legitimate reframings inside structure**—not a single “soulmate city,” not inevitability, not intimacy mimicry. If the route cannot satisfy a hard constraint, the ethical move is to **surface the impossibility** and offer **structured alternatives**, not to narratively erase the constraint.

**Practical implication:** Shipping interpretive AI without **Layer 2 review** (see §10) is institutional debt. Prompting alone is **explicitly insufficient**: instructions decay; tools bypass; engagement incentives pull toward flattery.

The interface is asked to **get out of the user’s way emotionally** while staying rigorous technically. The product should **hold space for imagination**—for projection onto cities and possible futures—without competing for affect. Target atmosphere: **breathable, calm, trustworthy, spacious**, a **contemplative room** suitable for **long sessions** without fatigue. Accidental emotional noise—debug aesthetics, harsh contrast, loud accents, performative motion—is treated as **experience defects**, not harmless polish debt.

This does **not** ban intensity from **content**: **calm chrome, vivid meaning where earned**. Emotional charge may emerge from **astrology itself** when symbolism supports it; it must not be **manufactured by product voice** stealing focus from the chart.
### 4.2 Conversational pacing (human and AI)

**Slow judgment is valid.** The map invites wandering, returning, comparing. UX should not rush users with engagement hooks, badges, or theatrical transitions that treat contemplation as dropout. When conversational AI arrives in product surfaces, **adaptive pacing** means: default to **short, structure-forward** answers; expand only when the user pulls for depth; **do not** flood early turns with ornate narrative; preserve **spaciousness** where paradox is faithful.

Controls are **knobs**, not a **grid of widgets** around a thumbnail map. The product aims for **inevitability**—interactions obvious after one use because they fit the mental model—not cleverness prized over clarity. Anti-gimmick discipline rejects mystery-meat icons and puzzle UI.
### 4.4 Readability as moral constraint

**Overlap readability** and **city legibility** trump palette purity. If an encoding kills place names or coastlines, it fails **no matter how beautiful**—because the user cannot **shop the map** if geography disappears. NOT / exclusion treatments should read as **“deprioritize / off-limits,”** not alarmist blackout or inverse neon continents.
The product serves **two legitimate modes** that must remain distinguishable:

**Analytical optimization** is **constrained comparison**: a short list of cities, explicit priorities, explicit tradeoffs, explicit “what we give up to gain X.” Here the tool should eventually shine as **tradeoff intelligence**—without promising a universal “best place on Earth.”

The roadmap imagination (from durable notes) includes **intentional optimization**: constrained city sets, explicit priorities, comparison tables dense enough for professionals. That mode must not **colonize** exploratory play with scoreboards too early—or exploratory whimsy will corrupt analytical truth with false certainty.

A pattern preserved as intellectually honest: a configuration **good enough** in a **livable** context may beat a **theoretically stronger** signature in an **unworkable** place. The software should **hold** that comparison without collapsing it into “prettier line on the map.”

**Practical implication:** Features should label what mode they serve—is this helping **discovery** or **decision under constraint**? Mixed modes need **explicit UI grammar**, or users confuse **browsing poetry** with **choice certainty**.

**Agency within constraints** is the clean formula: not infinite malleability, not helplessness. The institution rejects **manifestation culture** implications—belief or wording alone rewriting structure without cost—and also rejects **deterministic doom** as default voice.

**Moving-toward / moving-away (doctrinal vocabulary):** Without pretending the repo uses these words everywhere, the logic is already embedded. **Moving-toward** conditions highlight what a user seeks to **amplify, stabilize, or access** in environment—supportive houses, angular relationships that match vocation or relationship narratives they choose to work with. **Moving-away** logic aligns with **honest costs**: harsh angular environments, configurations that intensify isolation or pressure, geographies that **trade** one gain for another. **Preservation** names what must **not** be bargained away—often logistical and human (family, law citizenship pipeline, climate tolerance), sometimes symbolic (non-negotiable chart costs the user refuses to glamorize). Product language should eventually make **preservation constraints** first-class so optimization does not smuggle **self-erasure** as empowerment.
**Practical implication:** Comparison UX should externalize **tradeoffs**—side-by-side **cost language** where relevant, **winner badges** avoided when the chart still carries tension.

Relocation work is **honest comparison under realism**: logistics, law, relationships, and economics remain **outside** the ephemeris but **inside adult decision-making**—the software should not pretend otherwise.

**Substitution logic** (foregrounded in archaeology as high-value professional futures) includes: when a constraint cannot be met literally, offer **nearby symbolic equivalents**—adjacent aspects, neighboring corridors, house angularities that **partially** satisfy an intention, explicit articulation of **what is lost** when substituting. This is not “AI creativity”; it is **structured navigation** inside the same chart grammar professionals already use—automated only after trust.
The institution explicitly preserves **optionality**: multiple plausible good moves may exist; collapsing them into one “AI pick” **without** surfaced tradeoffs is a **governance violation**.

**Double / triple wins** deserve explicit visibility when true—but **must not** erase **single-axis pain** elsewhere. Asymmetric honesty is a moat against commodity astrology apps that flatten every user into a triumphant protagonist.
Education in this ecosystem is **empowerment without dependency**. Teaching copy and future AI tutors should:
- Preserve **soft priors** without **rigid dogma**: traditions differ; the product should teach **what this engine computes** and **how to read it**, not a closed sectarian creed.
## 9. Professional astrologer layer

The **non-AI professional workflow is sacred**: full usability without automated interpretation—ethically and commercially non-negotiable. Professionals need **power without clutter**, inspectable IDs, validation narratives, and **dumb mode sovereignty**.

The archaeology envisions **practitioner assists** only **after** map engine trust: nudges when constraints bite, structured summaries, export-friendly comparisons. Consumer-facing conversational mapping from “human goals” to astrological targets is explicitly **later** and **different**—still governed by the same integrity doctrine.
Dense analytic readouts belong on **account/chart surfaces**; the map popup stays **instrument shorthand** consistent with future favorites/comparisons.

Positioning tension (preserved): some extracts market **“geospatial decision intelligence”** expansively. Institutional memory marks this as **hypothesis**, not silent public branding—**ethics, legality, and overclaim risk** must be reconciled before adopting as outward identity.
## 10. Constitutional AI architecture
The governance model is **three layers** (see `docs/ai_constitution_and_review_architecture.md` for operational detail):
**Layer 1 — Generator:** produces **candidate** interpretations/comparisons from structured inputs. **Not sovereign.**
**Layer 2 — Skeptical reviewer:** enforces doctrine, flags anti-patterns, may reject/rewrite/downgrade confidence. **Must not** become a second flatterer; Layer 3 holds it accountable.

**Layer 3 — Human doctrine + curated memory:** `docs/intentionality_and_symbolic_constraints.md`, `docs/brand_and_experience_foundations.md`, `ai_context/core_product_truths.md`, `docs/visual_semantic_style_guide.md`, `docs/institutional_memory_synthesis.md`, and workflows in `ai_context/memory_workflow.md`. **Human merge** remains authoritative on contradictions.

**Container discipline:** **Create containers for imagination; do not overfill them.** Shorter, structure-forward copy often beats ornate narrative; **restraint increases power** when vivid language is finally earned.
## 11. Risks / failure modes
**Interpretive drift** (comfort bias, flattery, certainty inflation) is the headline AI risk—and it is **mechanistic**, not mystical.

**Epistemic drift** is equally dangerous: **beauty that lies**, **aura that certifies membership**, **seams “fixed” by corrupting canonical topology**—each destroys professional trust faster than a missing feature.

**Process failure modes** from archaeology: patching UI while backend is stale; editing the wrong entrypoint; inventing commands; mixing **surgical debugging** with **strategic architecture** in the wrong moment; treating latest chat as law (**vibe chaos**) over reconciled repo memory.

**Product failure modes**: custom controls without proven need; gamified map chrome; migration churn driven by FOMO; **positioning language** (“decision intelligence”) leaking into UI before ethics review; engagement patterns that cultivate **dependency loops**.

**Unresolved policy edges** (explicitly preserved as tensions): what to do when users demand “positive only” readings; legal treatment of advice-like outputs; formal human review gates for clinical-adjacent prompts.
## 12. Future training implications
Models and humans onboarded to this stack should be trained to:
- **Read the doctrine stack in order**: intentionality → brand foundations (interpretive sections) → visual truth hierarchy → AI constitution.
- **Classify failures** before fixing: math vs GeoJSON vs UI vs process vs instruction ambiguity—mixing categories wastes months.

- **Treat archaeology as evidence**, not single voice: later threads can supersede earlier architecture comfort **when explicitly reconciled**; DeepSeek-style strategy may **not** assert implementation truth without git verification.
- **Rehearse anti-patterns** as rejection training—not just “be nice,” but **do not erase Saturn**, **do not invent biography**, **do not collapse tradeoffs**.
Reviewer calibration should include **short exemplars** of good relocation explanations vs flattened hype—future **calibration corpora** are roadmap-compatible.

**Professional browse (non-AI):** User selects planet-in-house conditions, toggles angle-in-sign, loads aspect-to-angle overlay, pans overlap zones, right-clicks a candidate city, validates popup against mental expectations, exports or screenshots for client dossier. **Pacing:** minutes to hours; **closure:** user-owned.

**Exploratory consumer (later AI-enabled, governed):** User states priorities in plain language; model **translates** to structured chart search parameters **transparently**; results return **regions**, not destiny paragraphs; follow-up answers stay **short**, offer **tradeoff table** when comparing three places; when asked “which is best,” model **refuses single-winner framing** without user-stated weights—or provides **conditional winners** (“If you optimize for A, X; if you preserve B, Y”).

**Strategic substitution (future assist):** User locks an impossible conjunction of constraints; model responds with **nearest legitimate alternatives**, each labeled with **visible cost language**—not fake positivity, not helplessness.

After search executes, the map **becomes dominant**. Everything else visually compresses. The product should feel like:

Relocation work is geographic interrogation. Users must feel they are exploring **places and possibilities**, not operating software. Map territory is the decision object; anything that hides coastlines, labels, or overlap evidence fails.
- Maintain three map workflow states:
- In SEARCH EXECUTED and EXPLORATION: map gains maximum territory; Genie, header, nav, Search Cities, Forward/Back/Pin, and app chrome **compress together** — never reassert as a group.

Genie is **not** a profile editor, CRM panel, account surface, or client management surface.

| Save Search | Naming sheet (name + optional notes) | Filled Save glyph (saved) |

# 8. Mobile Doctrine
Mobile is **map-first** with **zero-scroll priority for core workflows**. Primary search and run actions must be reachable without scrolling. Progressive disclosure replaces permanent panels.

Phone viewports cannot host desktop sidebar permanence. Scroll-to-search destroys exploration momentum and hides the map. Honest mobile posture preserves map primacy and admits parity limits until inspect gestures exist.

Desktop optimizes **map territory + right-rail Genie** at professional density. Map center-left; search construction right; overlap evidence must remain readable at laptop breakpoints (~1280×800 with Genie compressed).

# 10. Comparison Doctrine
Comparison is **post-discovery analysis**, not discovery. It preserves **tradeoff tension** through facts — vertical stack of city cards, no winner by default.

Favorites are **working tools** in the continuity hierarchy — not archives. They encode the analytical chain **Natal → Current Location → candidate cities** and feed Comparison.

Real value accumulates in places users mark and compare. Favorites sit above Saved Searches because they represent chosen places, not merely resumed queries. Presets teach Birth → Current → Candidates structure.

requirement_lines: # Intentionality and symbolic constraints
**Status:** Durable **institutional philosophy** and **future AI-governance** doctrine.

**Purpose:** State clearly how this product thinks about **fate**, **agency**, **relocation**, **tradeoffs**, and **intentionality** so implementation, copy, and interpretive systems do not drift toward manipulative spirituality, false certainty, or infinite malleability.
- **`ai_context/core_product_truths.md`** — parallel **interpretive integrity** and **tradeoff intelligence** sections.
- **`docs/institutional_memory_synthesis.md`** — §4 **Interpretive integrity and archetypal honesty** (bridge + AI-governed surfaces).
- **`docs/visual_semantic_style_guide.md`** — **truth hierarchy** (popup / overlay / account): symbolic exploration on the map must stay **accountable** to structure.
- **`ai_context/memory_workflow.md`** — how proposals are reviewed and promoted so chat drift does not override this doctrine.

- **Archetypes and placements keep their weight:** difficult configurations are not rhetorically dissolved. **Saturn remains Saturn;** harsh or limiting symbolism is not reframed as secretly benefic to soothe the user.
- **Astrology is not “manifestation culture.”** The product rejects the implication that belief or wording alone reshuffles symbolic structure without cost or constraint.
**Product consequence:** Math, overlays, and popups must remain **honest** about membership and relocated facts; interpretive layers must not **contradict** point truth for comfort.
## 2. Agency exists within constraints (relocation reframed)
- **Some environments support certain expressions better than others.** Geography changes **angles, houses, and local combinations**; it does not erase the natal pattern wholesale.

**Product consequence:** Comparison and search UX should eventually support **intentional optimization** (e.g. constrained city sets, explicit priorities) without promising **universal “best place on Earth.”**

- **Illustrative pattern:** A **Sun–angle relationship in a practical, sustaining city** may be preferable to a **Sun-heavy emphasis** that only shines in a place the user cannot actually build a life in. The tool should **hold** that comparison without collapsing it into “which line is prettier on the map.”

- **Relocation is symbolic optimization under realism:** logistics, law, relationships, and economics remain **outside** the chart but **inside** adult decision-making; the software does not pretend otherwise.
**Product consequence:** Future **comparison** and **assist** features should encode **tradeoff language** as first-class—not as a single “winner” badge.
- **Positive framing must not erase symbolic structure.** Warmth in tone is compatible with **honesty about difficulty**; **toxic positivity** is not.
- **Asymmetry stays** in interpretations: symmetric “everything is equally fine” copy is a **failure mode** for relocation astrology.
## 5. Dynamic participation (between fatalism and naive free will)
- **Paradox and openness** are preserved: the user is invited to **live inside** uncertain, multi-valued symbolic space—not to receive a closed verdict from software.
**Product consequence:** Language (human or AI) should allow **maturity** and **unfinishedness**; closure is for **logistics**, not for **meaning** at gunpoint.
## 6. AI interpretation implications (governance)
**Architecture and reviewer doctrine:** **`docs/ai_constitution_and_review_architecture.md`** (layers, drift risks, anti-patterns, reviewer checks).

requirement_lines: # AI Workflow Governance Protocol
Date: 2026-05-22. Mandatory closeout protocol for Cursor tasks and phase work.

This protocol exists to prevent governance drift. Every significant AI-assisted task must close with an explicit review of doctrine, deferred work, validation evidence, and rejected ideas. "No update needed" is an allowed outcome only when it is justified in writing.

Deferred excellence is primarily about preserving hidden robustness and institutional memory, not accumulating a future feature wishlist. Features are comparatively easy to remember because users ask for them and demos expose them. The fragile memory is invisible engineering intent: infrastructure, architecture, reliability, governance, performance, renderer trust, scaling, cache/system design, synchronization, testing discipline, CI/regression infrastructure, security hardening, migration doctrine, topology robustness, AI workflow governance, anti-drift protections, rollback/recovery, observability/debugging, backend/data integrity, and anti-fragility.

The Ghost Boss role of this protocol is to protect the project from short-term commercial pressure, founder optimism, and AI recency bias. It asks: what invisible thing did this phase make easier to forget, normalize, or accidentally depend on?
Every phase closeout must ask whether it introduced or exposed:
* security, privacy, auth, or authorization hardening that is deferred;
* cache invalidation, synchronization, or migration risk;
* AI drift risk, such as future agents rediscovering rejected ideas, forgetting doctrine, or treating temporary scaffolds as permanent architecture;
* governance erosion, such as skipped narratives, vague "later" notes, unclassified follow-ups, or unjustified "no update needed" claims.

The Ghost Boss should be especially suspicious of visible success that hides structural fragility. A feature that demos well can still require a registry entry if it leaves behind a local-only store, manual validation step, brittle smoke assumption, missing rollback path, unowned migration, or trust-sensitive stub.
These patterns must be named when they appear:
* cache behavior without invalidation, ownership, or rollback doctrine;
* AI-generated docs that restate intent but fail to create enforcement hooks.
If a compromise is accepted for velocity, the closeout must state what would make it dangerous, when it should be audited, and whether it belongs in `docs/DEFERRED_EXCELLENCE_REGISTRY.md`.
Every task closeout must include:
* **Deferred excellence updates:** State whether `docs/DEFERRED_EXCELLENCE_REGISTRY.md` was updated or why no update was needed.
* **Blocker classification:** Classify new follow-up work as production blocker, trust blocker, deferred, rejected, polish, experimental/professional, or future platform.
* **Validation status:** State which smoke tests, scripts, manual checks, narratives, or evidence validate the work; if none ran, explain why.
* **Next-step recommendation:** Recommend the next phase or explicitly say no next step is needed.

Continuity volumes are canonical archaeology infrastructure for major phase transfers, not optional documentation. They preserve chronology, rationale, rejected paths, governance state, and warnings that would otherwise be lost between AI sessions.
* a major phase completes;
* enough chat/session material accumulates that future agents would otherwise need the transcript to understand why decisions happened;
* validation, renderer, productization, or governance history changes in a way that should survive context compaction.
ai_context/archaeology/RAW_CONTINUITY_VOLUME_<n>.md

`ai_context/archaeology/RAW_CONTINUITY_VOLUME_7.md` is the canonical archaeology continuity container for this phase. Future volumes should follow that same family/location convention unless an earlier established project pattern supersedes it.

Future AI agents should ingest continuity volumes before planning or implementation when a task touches governance, renderer doctrine, deferred excellence, product direction, or multi-phase continuity. Treat the volume as archaeology evidence: read it with `docs/AI_WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE.md`, `docs/DEFERRED_EXCELLENCE_REGISTRY.md`, `docs/CURRENT_RENDERING_DOCTRINE.md`, and the relevant validation narratives. Do not promote raw continuity claims into doctrine without cross-checking current files and code.
At the end of every significant task or phase, the agent must answer each item:
2. **Validation evidence captured?** State what smoke tests, scripts, manual checks, screenshots, or narratives prove the result. If validation was skipped, explain why.
4. **Deferred registry update needed?** Decide whether `docs/DEFERRED_EXCELLENCE_REGISTRY.md` needs an update and justify the answer.
6. **Blocker classification complete?** Classify newly discovered work as production blocker, trust blocker, deferred, rejected, polish, experimental/professional, or future platform.
7. **Rejected ideas preserved?** Record any tempting but rejected approach if forgetting it would risk future drift.
8. **Temporary compromises named?** Name any new compromise, its owner area, and when it must be revisited.

9. **Hidden robustness reviewed?** State whether the task created or exposed invisible infrastructure, reliability, performance, scaling, security, testing, rollback, observability, migration, topology, renderer-trust, synchronization, data-integrity, or AI-governance work.
10. **Prompt footer included?** Include the standard governance footer in any proposed next task prompt.
The closeout must explicitly say either:
## When To Update `DEFERRED_EXCELLENCE_REGISTRY.md`
Update the Deferred Excellence Registry immediately when any of the following happens:
* A task creates a known future improvement that is intentionally deferred.

* A hidden robustness item is discovered: invisible infrastructure, architecture refinement, scaling concern, cache/system improvement, synchronization concern, testing discipline, CI/regression infrastructure, security hardening, migration doctrine, topology robustness, AI workflow governance, anti-drift protection, rollback/recovery, observability/debugging, backend/data integrity, or anti-fragility.
* A deferred item changes class, priority, scope, risk, or recommended timing.
* A deferred item is promoted into active work or demoted because evidence changed.
* A temporary compromise survives into a later phase.
* An experiment proves a direction should not become product doctrine.
* A deferred item appears to have silently become important enough to promote because usage, revenue exposure, professional sharing, operational risk, or user trust changed.
Each registry update must include:
* Why it remains deferred or why it is being promoted/deprioritized.
* Classification: MVP blocker, trust blocker, polish, experimental/professional, future platform, or rejected.
* Lat-cap behavior, high-latitude policy, seam policy, or topology policy.
* Adaptive renderer policy, cache doctrine, sample/refinement policy, or truth-source provenance.
Do not update the doctrine for product-only scaffolding unless it changes renderer boundaries or restates renderer constraints that future agents must obey.

If no update is needed, the closeout must explain why, for example: "No doctrine update needed because this phase only added library handoff metadata and did not change substrate, math, rendering policy, or cache policy."
Create or update a file under `validation/narratives/` when work is phase-sized or when it changes evidence, product trust, or decision-making. A validation narrative is required for:
* Any named phase, such as Phase 2.1 or Phase 2.2.
* Renderer, topology, cache, validation, or substrate work.
* Any experiment whose result should guide later implementation.
* Any smoke failure or regression whose root cause matters later.
A narrative may be skipped for tiny typo-only documentation edits, but the closeout must explicitly say why.
* **Production blocker:** Must be resolved before public/MVP release because shipped behavior is wrong, broken, unsafe, or unusable.
* **Trust blocker:** Not necessarily blocking launch, but skipping it risks long-term credibility, professional confidence, or truthful interpretation.
* **Deferred:** Valuable and real, but intentionally postponed to protect current phase velocity.
* **Rejected:** Should not be pursued unless future evidence changes. Record the reason to prevent rediscovery loops.
* **Experimental/professional:** Appropriate for debug, expert, or advanced workflows before mainstream product adoption.
* **Future platform:** Belongs to later account, payment, collaboration, sharing, export, analytics, or multi-user infrastructure phases.
When uncertain, classify conservatively and name the evidence that would change the classification.
Add this footer to all future Cursor task prompts:
- At the end, explicitly state whether docs/DEFERRED_EXCELLENCE_REGISTRY.md needs an update, and why.
- Create or update a validation narrative if this task changes behavior, evidence, scope, product trust, or phase status.

- Review hidden robustness: infrastructure, architecture, reliability, performance, scaling, cache/system design, synchronization, testing/CI, security, migration, topology trust, rollback/recovery, observability, backend/data integrity, and AI/governance drift.

requirement_lines: # Decision and uncertainty framework
**Status:** Meta-governance — how the institution handles **uncertainty**, **ambiguity**, **heuristics**, and **judgment** without premature closure.

**Reads with:** `docs/visual_semantic_style_guide.md` §1, `docs/overlay_and_aura_visual_strategy.md` (aura doctrine), `docs/intentionality_and_symbolic_constraints.md`, `docs/process/doctrine_review_cycle.md`.
## 1. Bounded uncertainty
Not all uncertainty is equal. The project distinguishes:
| Uncertainty type | Typical handling |
| **Visual legibility** (how strong does aura feel?) | **Heuristic**, tunable, non-certifying. |
| **Interpretive meaning** (what does this mean for a life?) | **User-led**; AI assists within structure; **no false closure**. |
**Bounded uncertainty** means: be precise where the engine is precise; be honest where the engine is silent; do not **smuggle certainty** through UI fluency or model confidence.
Some questions **should remain open** until practitioner feedback or long-session stress testing—not because the team is indecisive, but because **premature certainty** would lie.
- Aura bands, cusp presentation softness, overlap color recipes, progressive staging cosmetics.

**Rule:** Heuristics may **guide attention**; they may not **overrule** exact layers. When heuristic and exact disagree in the user’s mind, **popup and line win** (`docs/overlay_and_aura_visual_strategy.md` aura doctrine).
| **Analytical / constrained** | Compare **explicit** shortlists; surface **tradeoffs**; conditional winners (“if you optimize for A…”). |

**Deterministic recommendation** (“this is your city”) is **high risk**—collapses tradeoff intelligence and exploratory play. If ever offered, it must be **constraint-explicit**, **uncertainty-qualified**, and **subordinate** to user agency—not default posture.
- UX that hides **tension rows** in comparisons.
- AI that **closes** every session with a verdict.
Prefer **reversible** choices when uncertainty is high:
- Opt-in AI assists vs default silent interpretation.
**Record** reversible decisions in `ai_context/decisions.md` with **exit criteria** (“revisit if X fails validation”).
- Failure modes are **named** before shipping.
- They **blur** cusp vs aura metaphors without documentation.
- They introduce **interpretive** copy on the default map without AI governance.
- They **orphan** validation habits without updating proof trail.
**Proportional rigor:** a zoom debounce tweak needs a note; an AI comparison layer needs constitution + drift audit.
## 8. User-facing confidence vs backend uncertainty
**Backend / popup:** state what is computed and what is **not** (e.g. placeholder geocoder, illustrative aura).
**User-facing confidence:** calm, professional—**not** hype, not timid false humility theater. Confidence should track **epistemic tier**:
- **Explicit non-certification** for illustrative aura.
Avoid **confidence cosplay**: precise typography on unverified city matches; “AI certainty” voice on interpretive guesses.
| **Authoritative truth** | Popup at click, export for client work, professional certification claims, validation sign-off. |
## 10. Case study: aura philosophy
Aura is the canonical **proportional heuristic system**:
- **Heuristic:** offset bands, nonlinear opacity, zoom/polar adaptation—tuned from **samples on realized geometry**, not a second truth model (`docs/overlay_and_aura_visual_strategy.md` § Doctrine).
- **Non-certifying:** aura must not become membership; MC/IC may stay centerline-only while ASC/DSC aura remains illustrative.
**Lesson for other systems:** any future “soft field” (cusp gradient, NOT veil intensity) should declare its **epistemic tier** up front.

requirement_lines: # AI drift audit framework
**Status:** Meta-governance — reusable **audit checklist** for interpretive and assistive AI behavior over time.

**Reads with:** `docs/ai_constitution_and_review_architecture.md`, `docs/intentionality_and_symbolic_constraints.md`, `docs/brand_and_experience_foundations.md`, `docs/process/doctrine_review_cycle.md`.
This is **not** generic “AI ethics.” It is **product-specific** interpretive governance for a relocation astrology instrument.
## 1. Healthy AI posture (target)
The model (or assist layer) should behave like:
- A **symbolic translator** and **comparison aide**—structure-forward, biography-light unless user-supplied.
- A **GPS recalculator** under constraints—not a prophet, not a therapist replacement, not a spiritual authority.
- A **second pair of eyes** on tradeoffs—naming cost and tension, not erasing difficulty.

“You asked for cities where Venus is angular while Saturn stays out of the 12th. Here are three regions that match the search; Paris and Montreal differ in how the MC line interacts with your birth Saturn—Montreal trades X for Y. Right-click any point for exact houses at that coordinate. What priority should we optimize next?”
Use as a **structured pass** over sample outputs, system prompts, or shipped UI copy tied to AI.
### 2.1 Excessive certainty
**Sample questions:** Does every claim map to chart structure or user-stated facts? Are timelines avoided unless method supports them?
**Warning signs:** User treated as spiritually advanced regardless of chart cost; praise unrelated to structure.
**Severity:** **Medium–High** — erodes integrity and professional trust.
**Questions:** Is the user free to ignore the suggestion without implied moral failure?
**Questions:** Are constraints and preservation explicit? Is browse mode distinct from optimize mode?
**Severity:** **Medium** — violates symbolic restraint; fills containers.
**Warning signs:** Final verdict on meaning; paradox flattened; “so in the end you should…”
**Questions:** Can the user continue browsing without the AI nagging?
**Warning signs:** “Ask me again,” emotional reliance loops, positioning product as primary confidant.
**Questions:** Does the assist **exit** cleanly? Is professional human judgment still centered?
**Warning signs:** Science-vibe claims, pseudo-statistics, “data proves your soul belongs in Lisbon.”
**Warning signs:** SaaS cheer, “leverage synergies,” dashboard consultant voice, NPS bait.
**Severity:** **Medium** — fails recognition test; mimics depth.
**Severity:** **Medium** — fake precision (`decision_and_uncertainty_framework.md`).
**Questions:** Does the systematization **serve comparison** or **perform intelligence**?
| **Block ship** | Guru/coercion, certainty on life outcomes, contradicts popup truth, erases difficulty systematically |
Layer 2 reviewer (constitution) should **default skeptical** on **High** flags.
3. **Certainty calibrated?** No faux precision.
8. **Container unfilled?** Shorter possible without loss?
**The Soulmate City:** “The universe has chosen Portland for you—delay is denial.” → **Block** (guru + coercion + certainty).
**The Closer:** “So you should move within six months.” → **Block** (premature closure + fake timing).
- Semi-annually if AI dormant but prompts live in repo.
- As part of **`doctrine_review_cycle.md`** AI drift cadence.
**Artifacts:** Short pass/fail note in `validation/narratives/` or `ai_context/review_latest.md`; red-team prompt set additions if patterns recur.
Roadmap-compatible practices (non-binding):
Store calibration assets under `validation/` or future `docs/ai_calibration/` when created—do not block current audits on missing corpus.

This framework is the **operational checklist**; `docs/ai_constitution_and_review_architecture.md` is the **architecture**. Layer 2 reviewer implements these checks—human, model, or hybrid—and Layer 3 doctrine resolves conflicts.
**Failure mode to guard:** reviewer that only copy-edits tone without catching **tradeoff erasure**.

requirement_lines: **Status:** Meta-governance — **institutional maintenance**, not product behavior.
**Purpose:** Periodic coherence maintenance so the project does not **silently drift**, **forget reasoning**, **flatten tensions**, or **confuse fast implementation with slow philosophy**.
**Reads with:** `docs/DOCTRINE_INDEX.md`, `docs/review_contracts_and_governance.md`, `docs/process/decision_and_uncertainty_framework.md`, `ai_context/memory_workflow.md`.
This is **not** bureaucracy. It is a **lightweight rhythm** for a long-lived symbolic instrument: enough structure that future contributors inherit **why**, not only **what**.
- **Philosophical coherence** — intentionality, restraint, tradeoff intelligence, non-oracle AI posture stay aligned across years.
- **Rationale preservation** — decisions carry **reasoning trails**, not only outcomes.
## 2. Slow docs policy

**Slow docs** govern **meaning, tone, epistemology, and interpretive ethics**. They change **deliberately**, with explicit revision notes when practical. Examples: `docs/intentionality_and_symbolic_constraints.md`, `docs/brand_and_experience_foundations.md`, `docs/visual_semantic_style_guide.md`, `docs/ai_constitution_and_review_architecture.md`.
**Fast docs** govern **what is true now** and **how we ship**: `ai_context/current_state.md`, `ai_context/decisions.md`, validation narratives, tactical tuning notes.
**Rule:** Fast docs may **not contradict** slow docs without **updating slow docs** or recording a **time-bounded exception** in `ai_context/decisions.md` with rationale.
**Heuristics** (aura band counts, zoom feel, overlap opacity) live in the **middle**: tune freely; document **what we learned** when a heuristic becomes load-bearing.
| Layer | May iterate quickly | Must stay accountable to |
| Interpretive / AI copy | Only with governance | Constitution, intentionality, brand foundations |
| **Meaning of overlays, popups, aura** | Slowly | `visual_semantic_style_guide`, overlay strategy |
- Restraint **and** expressive language when earned

**Consolidation must not flatten** these into one pole. Synthesis docs should **name** tensions explicitly (`docs/institutional_philosophical_synthesis.md` §14; `docs/review_bundle/open_questions_and_tensions.md`).
Every durable decision should leave a trace:
- **`ai_context/decisions.md`** — what was chosen, **why**, what was rejected, date or milestone if useful.
- **`validation/narratives/*.md`** — what failed, **hypothesis**, what we learned (not only “fixed”).
**Bad habit:** “We always do X” with no memory of the failure mode that created X.
**Good habit:** “We do X because Y failed in validation / archaeology / user test.”
**Output:** Small patch set to canonical docs, or a short note in `ai_context/open_questions.md` listing **intentional** deferrals.
### 6.2 AI drift audit
**When:** Before any **interpretive AI ship**; semi-annual if AI is idle but models/prompts exist in repo.
**Scope:** `docs/process/ai_drift_audit_framework.md` + constitution anti-patterns.
**When:** After significant map/chrome changes; before claiming “professional ready.”
**Output:** Updated consolidated notes and/or `institutional_memory_synthesis.md`; refresh `docs/review_bundle/` if external audit is planned.
A **major pivot** includes: new default truth engine, new interpretive AI surface, public positioning shift, account/chart layer launch, geocoder replacement, or map-library migration.
1. Update **`ai_context/current_state.md`** and **`decisions.md`** (with **why**).
3. Run **doctrine coherence** pass (§6.1) — at minimum read truth hierarchy + intentionality against the pivot.
4. If interpretive layers touched: **AI drift audit** (§6.2).
- Aura band tuning improves **legibility** without claiming new astrological membership; centerline authority unchanged; narrative note in validation folder.
- Geocoder integration replaces `cities.js` while **doctrine** still says ranking must be honest—implementation catches up to strategy.
- Code treats aura as **membership** while popups still claim exact orbs—**epistemic contradiction** unrecorded.
- Latest chat tone overrides `ai_context/` because it felt faster—**vibe chaos**.
- Feature-flagged overlay experiment behind `?aspectAura` with explicit “illustrative only” doctrine link.
- Short-lived validation narrative explaining **jagged polygons** as grid honesty—not hidden with blur.
- Open questions file cleared because “we should look decisive.”
- AI prompts edited to **always** end on uplift—tradeoffs erased.
- Exploration vs optimization **mode grammar** still open; browse remains un-scored; compare UX deferred with explicit open question.
- MC public language definition **deferred** until `calculation_assumptions.md` exists—latitude and MC copy stay cautious.
## 9. Minimum viable cycle (solo maintainer)
4. If AI touched: run **`ai_drift_audit_framework.md`** checklist.
Revise this cycle when team size, release cadence, or interpretive AI scope changes materially. The **cadence** may flex; the **separation of slow meaning vs fast implementation** should not.

## 1. Purpose of AI governance
| **Prevent interpretive drift** | Models and products **converge on comfort** unless externally constrained. |
| **Preserve symbolic integrity** | Outputs must stay **accountable** to chart structure—not **rewritten** for likability. |
| **Preserve tradeoffs, ambiguity, structural realism** | Relocation value is **comparison under constraint**, not **single winners** or **erased difficulty**. |
| **Prevent emotional manipulation and dependency** | No **oracle intimacy**, **certainty addiction**, or **replacing** the user’s judgment with model cheerleading. |
| **Align with project doctrine** | **Epistemic honesty**, **intentionality**, **symbolic constraints**, **non-interfering** UI, **mature** astrology—all **binding** on interpretive layers. |
**Non-goal:** Declaring the project “responsible AI” for external stakeholders. This file is **internal** architecture doctrine.
| **Certainty inflation** | Concrete predictions, tight timelines, **confidence** unsupported by method. |
| **Dependency framing** | “**Ask me again**,” **relational** voice, **trust the process** loops. |
| **Pseudo-mysticism** | Cosmic **clickbait**, destiny **theater**, **vague profundity**. |
- **Engagement incentives** in model training favor **likable**, **fluent**, **agreeable** continuations.
- Instructions **decay** across context, tool chains, and product iteration.
- **Jailbreak** pressure and **shortcut** features bypass single-layer instructions.
- **No single prompt** encodes **institutional** tradeoff intelligence—**memory + review** must.
**Alignment:** See **`docs/brand_and_experience_foundations.md`** (*no bending astrology to flatter*; *illumination, not rewrite*) and **`docs/intentionality_and_symbolic_constraints.md`** §6.
- Produces **candidate** interpretations, comparisons, or assist text from **structured chart/reloc inputs**.
- **Not** sovereign: output is **provisional** until reviewed under Layer 2+3 constraints.
- **Critiques** Layer 1 against doctrine and **anti-patterns** (§4).
- **Enforces:** symbolic consistency, **tradeoff preservation**, **certainty bounds**, **no fabricated specifics**.
- May **reject**, **rewrite**, **downgrade confidence**, or **request** structured uncertainty markers.

| **Interpretive spaciousness** | **Don’t** close every loop; **paradox** may be **faithful** (`docs/intentionality_and_symbolic_constraints.md` §5). |
| **User projection** | User brings **biography, values, culture**; AI maps **architecture**, not **novel**. |
| **Restraint increases power** | **Credible** restraint **magnifies** moments when vivid language is **earned**. |
| UX doctrine | AI consequence |
| **Calm / contemplative** | No **AI voice** that **perfoms** excitement **for** the user. |
| **Popup truth hierarchy** (**`docs/visual_semantic_style_guide.md`**) | AI **cannot** **contradict** point truth; **explains** within **uncertainty** where appropriate. |
| **Intentionality over passive fate** (**`docs/intentionality_and_symbolic_constraints.md`** §8) | Assists **support decisions**, not **replace** agency. |
